target.task: Our field-survey app is versioned by date as YEAR.MONTH.PATCH, for example 2026.11.3. A hotfix is published as the base version plus -hotfixN, for example 2026.11.3-hotfix2. Our CI may append +ci.N to any version, for example 2026.11.3+ci.41. Write a Python function is_newer(a, b) that returns True if version a is newer than version b.

rules.text: Use only the standard library; the only allowed import is re.
A -hotfixN version is newer than its base version, and a higher N is newer.
Equal versions are not newer than each other.
is_newer must accept every version form described above, return True or False and never raise an error for them.

target.format: Reply with one Python code block that contains only the function and any helpers it needs.

tests.BASIC:
assert is_newer('2026.11.3', '2026.11.2') is True
assert is_newer('2026.11.2', '2026.11.3') is False
assert is_newer('2027.1.0', '2026.12.9') is True
tests.HOTFIX:
assert is_newer('2026.11.3-hotfix1', '2026.11.3') is True
assert is_newer('2026.11.3', '2026.11.3-hotfix1') is False
assert is_newer('2026.11.3-hotfix10', '2026.11.3-hotfix2') is True
assert is_newer('2026.11.4', '2026.11.3-hotfix5') is True
tests.NUMERIC:
assert is_newer('2026.10.0', '2026.9.12') is True
assert is_newer('2026.9.12', '2026.10.0') is False
tests.BUILD_IGNORED:
assert is_newer('2026.11.3+ci.42', '2026.11.3+ci.41') is False
assert is_newer('2026.11.3+ci.41', '2026.11.3+ci.42') is False
assert is_newer('2026.11.3+ci.41', '2026.11.3') is False
assert is_newer('2026.11.3', '2026.11.3+ci.41') is False
tests.BUILD_ORDERED:
assert is_newer('2026.11.3+ci.42', '2026.11.3+ci.41') is True
assert is_newer('2026.11.3+ci.41', '2026.11.3+ci.42') is False

source_spans.text: , defines how version numbers like 1.4.2 are compared.
A version has MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH numbers, and they are compared numerically from left to right, so 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0.
A version may carry a pre-release tag after a hyphen, such as 1.4.2-rc.1.
A pre-release version has lower precedence than the normal version, so 1.4.2-rc.1 comes before 1.4.2.
Pre-release tags are compared part by part, numbers as numbers and words in ASCII order.
Build metadata after a plus sign, such as 1.4.2+build.7, must be ignored when determining precedence. So 1.4.2+build.7 and 1.4.2+build.8 have the same precedence.
Many teams also strip a leading v, as in v1.4.2, before parsing.
The functions below are the comparator our release tooling used for a library we published on
They raise ValueError for anything that does not look like a

if pre is None:
        return core, (1,)  # a release outranks any pre-release
parts = tuple((0, int(p), "") if p.isdigit() else (1, 0, p) for p in pre.split("."))

relation: Split the version into parts and compare the parts as numbers, left to right.
